# General Rundown
Several companies across different states receive funding from pharmaceutical companies to test their drugs.
Within clinical trials, there are multiple phases for testing these drugs. This discussion focuses exclusively on healthy volunteer clinical trials, which are designed for individuals without major health conditions who are generally in good health.
It's important to note that "generally good health" does not require being in peak physical condition. Instead, your vital signs are assessed before entering a clinical trial to ensure they fall within healthy ranges.
For example, an ECG is performed while you lie down to monitor your heart rate. Blood pressure is also measured, with each study specifying acceptable ranges for measurement. The typical maximum acceptable blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, although some studies may accept individuals with slightly higher readings. Don't assume you cannot participate in a study if your blood pressure is above this threshold; however, it is advisable to aim for a maximum of 140/90 mmHg to qualify for any study.
Additionally, a urine sample is collected to test for pregnancy (for women) and drug use (for both men and women). Your height and weight are recorded to verify your BMI, and approximately 10 cc of blood is drawn, which is not a lot of blood, it would not be considered a blood donation. These tests are straightforward.
You will also be asked about your medical history and any past injuries, and your responses will be taken at face value. These assessments help determine whether you are considered a healthy individual.
Lastly, individuals taking non-prescription over-the-counter medications (such as multivitamins) or prescription drugs are not accepted. Stop taking any over-the-counter medications in advance to ensure they do not appear in your urine or blood tests.
# Finding Clinical Trial Companies
To locate clinical trial companies, start with your state or the nearest state to minimize travel costs, as most companies do not cover travel and lodging expenses. Many states conduct clinical trials, so finding trial companies should not be difficult.
Once you identify a potential trial site, visit their website to see what clinical trials are available for healthy volunteers/phase one trials. Ensure that the website lists "phase one" or "healthy volunteers." You will likely find multiple trials available. The website will provide options to fill out a contact form or call them. Even if you complete the contact form, I recommend calling the trial company, as competition for spots can be high.
When selecting a trial to apply for, if you need the money urgently, choose the trial that offers funds the soonest. Generally, aim for trials that pay between **5,000 and 8,000 dollars** and require no more than two months of visits or stays. This approach allows you to maximize your earnings throughout the year. While trials offering significantly higher payments are appealing, be cautious of those that pay but last an entire year.
Keep in mind that there is a 30-day washout period between trials. After completing a clinical trial, you must wait 30 days from the last date you were dosed before participating in another trial. This waiting period ensures that any medication tested is flushed from your system, preventing it from affecting the results of subsequent trials. Most clinical trials utilize a database company (VCT) to track the last time you were dosed, helping to prevent participation before the washout period. However, not all clinical facilities use this system.
During the phone call, you will be asked about your contraception method, height, and weight. Some studies may have specific requirements regarding BMI or contraception methods. When contacting a trial company, you should request to speak with a recruiter for healthy volunteer studies. The purpose of the call is to determine if you pre-qualify for a study.
If you qualify, you will be scheduled for an in-person screening to check your vitals. If you pass this initial check, you will be tentatively selected for the trial. A final vitals check will occur on the day of check-in for the study. If you pass this last assessment, you are officially in! During the trial, you will receive free housing and food. Keep in mind, trials will overbook qualified participants, “alternates,” just in case someone does not pass the day of check-in. If selected as an alternate you receive a reduced payment. Paid for the number of days you participated and sent home early.
Be sure to inquire beforehand about payment methods and the frequency of payments. Some trial companies may pay you weeks after the trial concludes, which could pose a financial burden.

HVAC stands for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning. It refers to the technology and systems used to control the indoor environment of buildings, ensuring comfort and air quality.
Components of HVAC
Heating
This component involves systems that provide warmth to indoor spaces, typically through furnaces, boilers, or heat pumps. These systems can use various energy sources, including gas, electricity, or renewable energy.
Ventilation
Ventilation is the process of exchanging or replacing air in a space to improve indoor air quality. This can involve natural ventilation (using windows and vents) or mechanical systems (like exhaust fans and air handling units) that circulate air.
Air Conditioning
Air conditioning systems cool and dehumidify indoor air, making it comfortable during hot weather. These systems can be central (cooling the entire building) or localized (like window units or portable air conditioners).
Importance of HVAC
HVAC systems are crucial for maintaining a comfortable and healthy indoor environment, regulating temperature, humidity, and air quality. They play a significant role in energy efficiency and sustainability in buildings.

A threat is the potential danger that can cause harm (e.g., hackers, natural disasters).
A Vulnerability is weakness in a system that can be exploited (e.g., software bugs, misconfigurations).

**Market Size and Viability for a Small Business with a Population Size of 5 Million**
A market size of 5 million people can indeed support a successful service-based small business, provided certain conditions are met. Here’s a breakdown of the rationale behind this.
**Key Considerations for Viability**
1. Target Market Identification:If you can identify and effectively target a niche within this market, even a small portion can produce substantial revenue. For instance, if you target just 1% of the market, that’s 50,000 potential customers.
2. Service Demand:The success of a service-based business also hinges on the demand for your specific services. Consider whether the services meet a significant need, such as health, beauty, home services, or consulting.
3. Pricing Strategy:Higher-value services can yield greater revenue with fewer clients. If your service can charge $100 per session, for example, serving 50 clients per month can generate $5,000 monthly.
4. Competition:Evaluate the competitive landscape. A market that is underserved may present better opportunities than a saturated one, even within a population of 5 million.
5. Operational Costs:Consider the overhead involved. If operational costs are manageable, it’s feasible to sustain a profit. This includes rent, materials, staffing, and marketing.
6. Marketing and Outreach:Your ability to effectively market your services to the target audience impacts how well you can tap into the 5 million population. Utilizing digital marketing, social media, and community engagement can enhance visibility.
7. Scalability:Many service-based businesses have the potential to scale. As you build a customer base, you might introduce additional services or expand to new areas, resulting in increased profits.
8. Economic Environment:Factors such as economic health, disposable income levels, and consumer spending habits in the area can greatly affect business viability
**Conclusion**
A 5 million population is substantial enough to support a service-based small business, provided you have a clear understanding of your niche, the demand for your services, and an effective strategy for reaching your target customers. The key is to ensure your offerings align with market needs while managing operational costs to maximize profitability. With the right approach, it’s entirely possible to make a good living in this environment.

Chyme is a Clubhouse-style social audio Android app.
A live, drop-in audio platform where people join topic-based rooms to listen, raise hands, and speak—moderators control the stage while the audience casually discovers and hops between conversations in real time.
Social audio platforms connect people in live, drop-in audio “rooms” where conversations happen in real time.
Core concepts
- Rooms: Temporary audio spaces for a topic or event. Anyone can join as audience (listener) or participate.
- Stage / Speakers: The visible area showing current speakers and moderators. Speakers broadcast audio; moderators control the conversation.
- Audience / Listeners: Join rooms to listen, raise hands to speak, and react without speaking.
- Moderation controls: Mute/unmute, invite-to-stage, remove from room, and hand-raising queue.
- Clubs / Profiles: Persistent groups or user identities that follow interests and schedule recurring events.

The Classifieds Era Ended and What Replaced It, and What TIs Can Use Now
Craigslist changed local commerce forever: one simple, free classifieds site that let people buy, sell, rent, hire, and swap with almost no friction. Three decades later, that model still exists, but its cultural dominance has waned and poses a challenge for TIs.
Why Craigslist declined
Trust and safety: rising awareness of scams, fraud, and violent incidents made users demand identity checks, ratings, and moderationProfessionalization and regulation: hiring and housing markets grew more regulated; employers and platforms wanted vetted applicants, and landlords wanted verified listings.Network fragmentation: specialized apps and large social networks absorbed verticals (housing, goods, services), drawing both supply and demand away.Which platforms replaced Craigslist’s main sections
Buying & selling: Facebook Marketplace, OfferUp, Mercari, eBay, and Poshmark. These add profiles, ratings, social context, and app-first UX—reducing friction and perceived risk.Housing: Zillow, Apartments/.com, HotPads and Zumper for professional listings; Airbnb. These platforms prioritize verified listings, mapping, photos, filters, and rental workflows.Jobs & gigs: Indeed, LinkedIn, and specialized job boards for salaried/white-collar roles; Upwork and Fiverr for remote freelance; dedicated local job apps and staffing marketplaces for hourly work.Local services/labor: TaskRabbit initially popularized on-demand errands and odd jobs, but the marketplace evolved—more heavy-labor or contractor-style work has shifted to platforms like Thumbtack, Handy, local staffing apps, and niche labor marketplaces that handle vetting, insurance, and payments.Community & neighborly exchanges: Nextdoor and neighborhood Facebook groups added local context and verification, serving hyperlocal needs better than anonymous classifieds.Notable differences in the new ecosystem
Identity and reputation: Profiles, reviews, and social graphs replaced anonymity—users trade some privacy for trust.Integrated payments and dispute resolution: App-native payments (Venmo/Zelle integrations, escrow, in-app checkout) cut down on risky cash meetups.Vertical specialization: Specialized platforms (real estate portals, job boards, resale apps) optimize for industry needs—screens for applicants, credit checks for rentals, shipping and returns for goods.Consequences for users and local economies
Safer transactions but higher fees and less serendipity: Users get security and convenience, but platforms often charge commissions or promote paid listings.Reduced anonymity and discoverability: Casual, free posts that reached wide local audiences are harder to replicate—good for compliance, worse for spontaneous exchanges.Labor market shift: Informal hiring moved into platforms that demand classification and compliance, which can improve worker protections but also increase costs and gatekeeping.Fragmented attention: Sellers and hirers now need multiple apps to reach a broad audience, fragmenting markets that Craigslist once unified.Is Craigslist dead?
Craigslist still exists and retains traffic in many categories, especially in smaller markets and for sellers who prefer zero-friction, no-fee listings. But its role as the default, catch-all classifieds network has diminished. The market is split into specialized, trust-oriented, mobile-first services—each optimized for a particular vertical or user need.
What this means going forward for TIs
The consequences for the lack of classified ads for the general population mentioned above apply to TIs as well; however, the biggest issue we face is the gatekeeping. With the splintering of services, it enables the Speceterati to more efficiently mob TIs out of opportunities.

However they know (or learn) their limitations and operate within them to avoid crackdowns by the state or federal level authorities. That’s more exploitation and symbiosis than actual “ruling.”

External intervention is usually a byproduct of internal resistance rather than a substitute.
- Empirically, many major liberations (e.g., slave revolts, resistance movements, uprisings against genocidal regimes) were driven by the oppressed organizing and acting for their own freedom rather than waiting for outside saviors.
- Relying on those insulated from harm or those who profit from the system is often ineffective; incentives and risk exposure matter in whether outsiders will act.
- Framing and clarity of goals matter: asking “who do I go to to end this?” is different from asking “who will free me?” The former implies seeking allies or mechanisms, the latter assumes an external rescuer.
- Practically, for people experiencing targeted harm, peer networks (others with lived experience), organized collective action, and evidence-based documentation are realistic starting points — safer, more credible, and more immediately actionable than assuming broad public or institutional rescue.
- Caveat: historical examples also show outside pressure (alliances, sympathetic movements, legal reforms, international intervention) can be decisive when combined with internal resistance; so a mixed approach can be effective when feasible. However, I do not know any examples where there is no internal resistance presence which leads me to believe external intervention is a byproduct of the oppressed work toward freedom.

The Specterati's Money laundering vs. TI Skills Economy’s circular economy — why they’re not the same thing
Money laundering hides the origin of funds so illicit cash looks legitimate. It’s a deliberate, often criminal process of layering transactions, moving money through shell companies or opaque services, and finally integrating it back into the economy as “clean” money. The goal is secrecy and personal gain.
A circular economy, by contrast, is about resource efficiency and community resilience. It keeps materials and skills in use longer through repair, reuse, sharing, and local services — reducing waste, cutting costs, and strengthening local supply chains. Transparency, sustainability, and collective benefit are core principles, not concealment.
Why that matters for the TI Skills Economy (TSE)
Legitimacy: TSE’s model — connecting people who offer repair, transport, and services — is built on visible, reciprocal exchanges, not hidden financial manipulation.Resilience: By keeping skills and materials circulating locally, TSE reduces dependence on outside systems and builds practical autonomy for TIs.Ethics and trust: The circular approach fosters accountability and solidarity, while money laundering undermines trust and exposes legal risks.Join the TI Skills Economy If you want practical, transparent ways to regain autonomy — trade skills, find local services, and strengthen community supply chains — join TSE. title: Price Increase and Sustainability Update for TI Skills Economy

Price Increase and Sustainability Update for TI Skills Economy

I'm writing to share an important update about the TI Skills Economy app's pricing and sustainability. Effective March 1, 2026, the subscription price will increase from $1/month to $2/month (or $24/year).

What This Means for You
If you're already a member, your pricing is locked forever. This change has no impact on you.

If you have not signed up yet, now is the time, so you too can have the $1/month forever pricing.

This is a commitment I'm making to our community. As long as you keep your account active—even if you're not using the app regularly—you'll continue paying the same amount you signed up for. You never have to worry about price increases. If you need to step away, you can leave your account open without paying anything and return later at your original rate.

New members signing up March 1st, 2026 or later, will pay the new rate. Your pricing locks in on the day you join, so you'll always know exactly what you're paying. I choose forever pricing and an affordable rate as a thank you to showing your support early on. And for being pioneers of the world's first psyop-free economy.

Why This Increase Matters
I want to be transparent about what's happening behind the scenes. Without this price increase, the app will go offline. The hosting costs are no longer sustainable on the current pricing structure, given the Specterati interference and harassment.

When the app goes offline, we lose something critical: new people can't sign up and discover this resource. Every day the platform isn't available, potential members in our community miss the opportunity to connect, build skills, and support each other.

How You Can Help (In Any Way You Can)
I understand that we are all survivors of human trafficking and trafficking-related trauma. Not everyone has the financial means to contribute, and that's okay. Here's how you can help, whatever your situation:

If You Can Contribute Financially
Please consider upgrading to the new $2/month rate or making a one-time contribution. Every dollar directly extends the time the app stays online and accessible.

If You Can't Contribute Financially
Please help us grow. Upvote and comment on Quora posts about the TI Skills Economy. Share your genuine experience using the app. More visibility means more members, which makes the platform sustainable for everyone. Your voice matters.

If You're Using the App but Struggling Financially
*Keep using it*. I'm committed to covering costs for those who genuinely cannot pay—I'm donating plasma to generate additional funds, and I'll continue to do whatever it takes.

The Bigger Picture
Right now, we have 60 members with 33 active. That tells me this app is needed. But we can't grow if the platform keeps going offline.

When we have enough funding, the app stays online, and new members can join. When we don't, it goes offline temporarily. Each cycle we miss is a missed opportunity to reach someone who desperately needs this community.

Your contribution—whether financial, through spreading the word, or simply by staying engaged—directly impacts whether this platform survives and thrives.

Thank you for being part of this community! Together, we can make the TI Skills Economy sustainable.

Targeted Individual.

Psyop-Free Economy

Survivors
The default descriptor for platform users in UI and editorial content. Preferred over "victims" in all contexts except legal or statutory references.

Live, Work, and Prevail
The core mission line of Charging the Future.

Specterati Lexicon

Specterati describes the organized harassment network using language grounded in their actual behavior: a dopamine-exploitation harassment economy funded through money laundering via the global economy. The terminology below replaces colloquial labels such as "gang stalking" and "gang stalker."

Specterati

- -ati: a suffix denoting a group or collective, suggesting a network working together.

A pervasive influence that spreads fear and control.

A powerful, unseen entity that enforces compliance.

A destructive force that seeks to eliminate individuality and freedom.

A domain ruled by fear and intimidation.

A rise in sinister activity and dominance in society.

Other Terms

A play on "caught red-handed," emphasizing both guilt and embarrassment when a member of the Specterati panics upon being caught committing a crime.

title: From 62 to 384: Building a Real Economy Where We Live, Work, and Prevail
content:
From 62 to 384: Building a Real Economy Where We Live, Work, and Prevail
We have the potential to reach 5 million TIs (human trafficking survivors) who come together to reclaim our lives. But today, I want to focus on the power of right here, right now. We have 411 people in our Quora community. Of those, 62 have already stepped forward to join the mission. My goal is simple: to connect with 384 people who are ready to thrive. With 411Quora members, that milestone is not just possible—it is within our grasp.
But what does a circular economy actually look like when it starts with just 411 of us? Does it require high-tech skills or distant corporations? No. It requires the everyday skills we already possess.

The Power of Everyday Skills
If we apply our model of mutual support to this group of 411, the growth potential is profound. We aren't waiting for permission to succeed. We are building a self-sustaining loop of care and value right now.
 Total Economic Activity: In a fully realized state, this group (384–411 people) could generate $24.66 million in annual activity.
 The Service Engine: 70% of this ($17.26 million) comes from the services we provide each other. This is the heartbeat of our community.
 The Local Loop: The remaining 30% ($7.4 million) covers local goods, food, and essentials, keeping our resources close to home.
Real People, Real Value: What You Can Earn
Imagine a community where another TI’s skills become your lifeline, and your skills become theirs. This isn't about abstract numbers; it's about dignity and connection. Based on our economic model, here is what a sustainable income looks like for three essential roles in our 384-person community:
 The Caregiver: One of us provides daily support and companionship to an elderly neighbor or someone recovering from trauma. Working a steady 25 hours a week at a community rate of $25/hour, this caregiver earns $32,500 in ServiceCredits annually. This income secures their housing and well-being, while ensuring their neighbor is safe and cared for.
 The Mechanic: Another member fixes cars for the community. Instead of paying a distant chain, neighbors pay in ServiceCredits. Working 30 hours a week at $35/hour (reflecting the specialized skill and tool costs). This mechanic earns $54,600 in Service Credits annually. This allows them to buy parts, upgrade their tools, and support their family, knowing their work keeps the whole community moving.
 The Babysitter: A parent offers childcare to other parents in the group, allowing them to work or rest. Working 15 hours a week at $20/hour. This babysitter earns $15,600 in Service Credits annually. This flexible income builds trust, frees up time for everyone to contribute more, and ensures the babysitter has the resources they need.

Note: ServiceCredits are not mandatory within the TI Skills Economy. You can offer free, barter, or fiat if desired. Learn more about ServiceCredits here:
https://youtu.be/KytNHghNtQ8

The Math of Connection
My commitment is to meet 384 TIs who are ready to be part of this.
 We have 411 people in this Quora community.
 We need 384 to say "yes."
 We have 62 who have joined.

This isn't a theoretical exercise. It is a reflection of our collective strength. Every time one of the 62 current members welcomes a new person, the economy grows. Every time we fix a car, watch a child, or care for a neighbor, the GDP rises.
Why 411 is Enough to Start

Some might say 411 is too small to matter. But history shows us that resilience begins in small, tight-knit groups.
 Authenticity: In a group of 411, we know each other. Trust is built on real interactions, not algorithms.
 Clarity: We can see exactly how our contributions help. We know who needs what, and we can act immediately.
 Unity: When we face challenges, we don't face them alone. We have a network of support that understands our journey.

The Path Forward
We are moving from surviving to prevailing.
1. Join now: If you are one of the 411, step forward. Your skills—whether fixing a sink, caring for a child, or listening to a friend—are vital: https://chargingthefuture.com.
2. Exchange Value: Offer a service. Accept a service. Keep the credits moving to strengthen our bond.
3. Grow Together: Once we stabilize at 384, we prove that we can thrive. Then we invite the next 1,000. Then 10,000. Then 5 million.
The future isn't built by waiting. It is built by 384 people, deciding that we are enough to start.

Are you ready to join the 384? Let's charge the future together.

EXIT THEIR ECONOMY, EXIT THE PSYOP: https://chargingthefuture.com.

It's important to note that "generally good health" does not require being in peak physical condition. Instead, your vital signs are assessed before entering a clinical trial to ensure they fall within healthy ranges.

For example, an ECG is performed while you lie down to monitor your heart rate. Blood pressure is also measured, with each study specifying acceptable ranges for measurement. The typical maximum acceptable blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, although some studies may accept individuals with slightly higher readings. Don't assume you cannot participate in a study if your blood pressure is above this threshold; however, it is advisable to aim for a maximum of 140/90 mmHg to qualify for any study.
Additionally, a urine sample is collected to test for pregnancy (for women) and drug use (for both men and women). Your height and weight are recorded to verify your BMI, and approximately 10 cc of blood is drawn, which is not a lot of blood, it would not be considered a blood donation. These tests are straightforward.

You will also be asked about your medical history and any past injuries, and your responses will be taken at face value. These assessments help determine whether you are considered a healthy individual.

Lastly, individuals taking non-prescription over-the-counter medications (such as multivitamins) or prescription drugs are not accepted. Stop taking any over-the-counter medications in advance to ensure they do not appear in your urine or blood tests.

Finding Clinical Trial Companies
To locate clinical trial companies, start with your state or the nearest state to minimize travel costs, as most companies do not cover travel and lodging expenses. Many states conduct clinical trials, so finding trial companies should not be difficult.

Once you identify a potential trial site, visit their website to see what clinical trials are available for healthy volunteers/phase one trials. Ensure that the website lists "phase one" or "healthy volunteers." You will likely find multiple trials available. The website will provide options to fill out a contact form or call them. Even if you complete the contact form, I recommend calling the trial company, as competition for spots can be high.

When selecting a trial to apply for, if you need the money urgently, choose the trial that offers funds the soonest. Generally, aim for trials that pay between 5,000 and 8,000 dollars and require no more than two months of visits or stays. This approach allows you to maximize your earnings throughout the year. While trials offering significantly higher payments are appealing, be cautious of those that pay but last an entire year.

Keep in mind that there is a 30-day washout period between trials. After completing a clinical trial, you must wait 30 days from the last date you were dosed before participating in another trial. This waiting period ensures that any medication tested is flushed from your system, preventing it from affecting the results of subsequent trials. Most clinical trials utilize a database company (VCT) to track the last time you were dosed, helping to prevent participation before the washout period. However, not all clinical facilities use this system.
During the phone call, you will be asked about your contraception method, height, and weight. Some studies may have specific requirements regarding BMI or contraception methods. When contacting a trial company, you should request to speak with a recruiter for healthy volunteer studies. The purpose of the call is to determine if you pre-qualify for a study.

If you qualify, you will be scheduled for an in-person screening to check your vitals. If you pass this initial check, you will be tentatively selected for the trial. A final vitals check will occur on the day of check-in for the study. If you pass this last assessment, you are officially in! During the trial, you will receive free housing and food. Keep in mind, trials will overbook qualified participants, “alternates,” just in case someone does not pass the day of check-in. If selected as an alternate you receive a reduced payment. Paid for the number of days you participated and sent home early.
Be sure to inquire beforehand about payment methods and the frequency of payments. Some trial companies may pay you weeks after the trial concludes, which could pose a financial burden.

content:

We've restructured how the wiki-blog content deploys to our public site. Previously, blog publishing relied on a fragmented pipeline that could create delays and inconsistencies. We've now unified the deployment process so that wiki-blog content flows directly from our main codebase to the live site through a single, dedicated channel.

title: Product Update: Security Hardening and Verification Flow (June 10, 2026)
content:
Product Update: Security Hardening and Verification Flow (June 10, 2026)

What Shipped

We merged three focused improvements to strengthen account security and clarify the verification process for members.

CSRF Protection on Mutation Routes
We hardened Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protections on sensitive account operations—specifically the account settings, mood tracking, and peer programming routes. This means your account changes are now validated more rigorously to prevent unauthorized modifications.

Unified Access Gate
We replaced a multi-version access system with a single, cleaner Unlock gate. This reduces complexity and makes permission checks more reliable across the platform.

Verification Clarity for Signed-In Members
Members who are signed in but haven't completed verification now see a prominent "Finish verifying" call-to-action on plugin landing pages. Support-only members see the normal Hub interface instead, improving the experience for different user roles.

Retired Feed Surface
We removed the legacy Feed app to streamline the codebase and reduce maintenance overhead.

Why It Matters

Security and clarity go hand-in-hand. When your account is protected by stronger validation, you can trust that your data and settings remain under your control. The clearer verification prompts remove friction—you'll know exactly what step comes next without guessing. These changes reflect our commitment to building a platform where survivors can work and collaborate with confidence, free from unnecessary complexity or risk.

The Add location button now gives you feedback. When you tap it, you'll see what happened instead of wondering if it worked.

Error logging is clearer. When something goes wrong, we now write errors to stdout so we can see them in Render logs. That means faster fixes when problems show up.

Design colors are locked in. We aligned the standard-theme plugin colors to match our canonical design table, so the look stays consistent.

ServiceCredits send panel is now full-width on mobile. No more cramped layouts when you're sending credits from your phone.

ClickLog works in production. We registered it in the plugin registry so it's available for everyone, not just in testing.

Why It Matters

These are small, practical fixes. They make the platform work better on the devices you actually use, give you clearer feedback when you take action, and help us spot and fix problems faster. Steady platforms let you focus on what matters to you.

title: ServiceCredits Monetary Policy Update
content:
ServiceCredits Monetary Policy Update

What Shipped

ServiceCredits now includes a full monetary policy layer. You can:
- View circulation metrics: See how many credits exist, how many are in use, and track the flow of value through the economy.
- Set mutual-credit limits: Each participant has a flat, equal limit on how much mutual credit they can use at once. No credit scores. No social ranking.
- Use the rail selector: Choose whether to earn credits through work, redeem them for services, or move them between accounts.
- Monitor the GDP boundary: The system enforces an upper limit on total credits in circulation to prevent inflation.

The dashboard gives you a clear view of all this. The debug agent now also surfaces structured error logs so you can see exactly what's happening when something goes wrong.

Why It Matters

A healthy economy needs transparency. When you can see how money moves and what the rules are, you're not guessing. You have control. These tools let you understand the system you're part of and make real decisions about how you participate.

Transparency in your network helps you understand what's actually happening around you. Seeing contribution signals without a numeric score means you get information without judgment or pressure. Platform parity means Android users have the same access as web users. These are small shifts toward a platform that works the way you need it to.

title: Product Update 2026 06 19 Honest Language and Chat Naming
content:

Foundation no longer says providers are vetted or background-checked. Foundation connects you with people who offer services. We don't run background checks. That's the honest description.

TrustTransport no longer claims to offer safety features or live tracking it doesn't have. TrustTransport coordinates rides. It doesn't have real-time location sharing or safety alerts. We took those words out.

We also named the two chat spaces in the platform:
- The Commons: the home chat where anyone can post to everyone. It's the many-voices space.

Skills Hunt works only if nominations connect to real, current data. These fixes close gaps between what the nomination interface shows and what the directory actually stores. The result is a nomination process that feels reliable—you submit a skill, it lands where it should, and the directory stays in sync.

title: Member Blocking and Safety Escalation
content:
Member Blocking and Safety Escalation

What Shipped

Two features rolled out together:

1. Block a member: Use the block option in the Commons or any Direct Line. Once blocked, that member can't send you messages or see your posts in shared spaces. You can unblock anytime from your Manage settings.

2. Safety escalation: When you block someone, you can optionally note that the block is tied to a safety concern. Moderators will see the flag and can review the context.

Why It Matters

Control over who reaches you is part of staying safe. Blocking is immediate and private—no one else sees your block list. If a block involves harassment or a threat, flagging it helps moderators spot patterns and keep the platform safer for everyone.

How to Use

To block a member:
- In the Commons: find their post or profile, tap the menu (three dots), select "Block."
- In a Direct Line: tap the member name at the top, select "Block."

To escalate a safety concern:
- When you block, a checkbox appears: "This block involves a safety concern." Check it if the reason involves harassment, threats, or suspicious behavior.
- Moderators receive the flag with your block. You don't need to add details unless you want to.

To unblock:
- Go to Settings → Manage → Blocked Members. Find the person and tap "Unblock."

Questions?

Reach out in the Commons or check the help section. The code is open at https://github.com/chargingthefuture/chargingthefuture if you want to see how it works.

Code-review sweep deduplication. The code-review sweep now remembers which findings it has already reported. When the same issue appears again, it won't create a duplicate report — it'll tag the existing one and move on. This keeps your audit trail clean and saves time.

Foundation instant-call push notifications on Android. When someone tries to reach you through a Foundation instant-call on mobile, your phone now sends a native push notification. You'll see the ring notification even if the app isn't open.

Code-review follow-up fixes. Audit contexts, deletion timestamps, and mobile auth gates got corrected across the workforce code-review flow. Mobile public pages and teaser stats now display correctly.

Why It Matters

The code-review sweep is built to catch issues over time. Deduplication means you're looking at actual new problems, not the same thing reported five times. That makes your audit easier to read and your fixes easier to track.

Push notifications on instant-call mean you're less likely to miss a message. The notification arrives whether or not you're in the app.

The fixes to timestamps, auth gates, and display states round out the code-review system so it works as intended across all surfaces.

title: Product Update — 2026-07-22
content:
Product Update — [number removed]

What Shipped

Edit button for Commons messages. Members can now edit their own posts in the Commons (home and #contributors channels) by clicking Edit next to Delete. Clicking Edit loads your text back into the composer, deletes the original message, and focuses the compose box so you can type your correction. When you send, it posts as a new message with a new timestamp — no silent in-place rewrites. Admins still have delete-any for moderation, but cannot edit someone else's message.

Chyme chat stays in place. Chyme's room interface now uses a fixed-height layout like Commons, so new chat messages scroll within the chat panel instead of pushing the entire page taller. The controls bar (Mute, Unmute, Raise Hand, Audio, Leave) moved to the top of the room, above the stage and chat, so the mute toggle is always reachable without scrolling.

In-app notifications jump to messages. Tapping "Open" on a notification now scrolls to and highlights the message in the Commons instead of just opening the panel. If the message is older than the recent-messages page, the app loads the surrounding window so you see it in context.

Web audio calls stay awake. While you're in a Chyme audio call on the web, the browser holds a screen wake lock so the display doesn't sleep and drop your call, and publishes Media Session presence to the OS so audio stays treated as active. (Native Android keeps its own foreground service; this is web-client only.)

Delete + repost is now the edit model everywhere. Message editing in the shared Stream chat (used by Foundation, Lighthouse, SocketRelay, TrustTransport, and Beacon) is now delete + repost, matching Commons and Chyme. In-place edits have been removed from that chat panel.

Mutual Time is in the admin grid. The admin landing page now includes a Mutual Time row pointing to /apps/mutual-time, where admins can create and manage polls.

Mutual Time code fixes. Audit lines now carry the policy decision that unlocked them. The admin event list rejects cross-origin requests. Vote counts are computed in a single query instead of one per event. The public vote view updates from the saved state instead of the load-time snapshot. Vote payloads must be strings, and unknown slots are rejected separately from bad payloads.

Test scripts updated. Commons (feed) and contributor-access are now tracked in the manual test-script drift gate, so feature inventory changes require matching test-script updates.

Username instructions clarified. The banner telling you to set a username now walks through the actual steps: click the person icon at top right, then Manage account, then edit your username.

Peer programming cohorts deduped. Weekly cohort assignments no longer include duplicate user IDs, keeping audit counts consistent.

Why It Matters

Editing is now consistent across the platform: a correction is always a fresh message with a new timestamp, so chat history stays honest and every change is visible and can be moderated. Chyme's layout fix makes audio calls less clumsy — you can mute without hunting for buttons. Notifications that actually jump to their target make the Commons easier to navigate. Small fixes to Mutual Time and the admin area remove friction from day-to-day use.

title: TSE Baseline
content:
This is a working document as I update the TSE app's baseline: chargingthefuture.com. Use it to learn my logic for what is implemented in the app. As well as an opportunity to provide feedback. I am only one person; multiple perspectives will make this economy better.

I am estimating 5 million TIs globally. The latest version of TSE uses Singapore as an example of where to start when it comes to facilitating an economy. I am now doing further research, and Finland might be a better option.

Examples of useful country targets with ~5M population (open data availability)
- Denmark (~5.9M) — excellent open stats (Statistics Denmark), strong circular policies.
- Finland (~5.5M) — high-quality datasets and open data portals.
- Norway (~5.4M) — rich public data (Statistics Norway).
- Slovenia (~2.1M), Latvia (~1.9M), Estonia (~1.3M) — smaller but very open data ecosystems and strong digital infrastructure (good for pilot scaling).
- Subnational regions: many cities/metro areas worldwide have populations of ~5M and publish detailed open data (transport, waste, land use).

Of the countries above or subnational regions, I propose the baseline of Finland (national) and two high-quality city/regional datasets (Greater Helsinki and Tallinn metro areas) as the primary model. This combination more closely aligns with creating a baseline for a hybrid (virtual and in-person) circular economy of human trafficking victims: some gated communities of survivors globally. And some that interact in a dispersed manner throughout the globe.

On March 29, 2026, I came across a writing about Estonia and its digital transformation. I will begin researching their implementation to see if there is anything we can integrate into TSE.

This document will be updated in the near future with more information.

title: Live, Work, and Prevail — a manifesto for survivors
content:
Live, Work, and Prevail — a manifesto for survivors

Who we are

We are survivors. Targeted Individuals (TIs) — people subjected to organized, long-running harassment carried out by what I call the Specterati: a coordinated network that profits from surveilling, isolating, and exploiting us. This is not a mystery and it is not spiritual warfare. It is organized crime — human trafficking — and it is old: I have found writing describing this same crime from the 1690s. I estimate at least five million of us worldwide. I am not suggesting we form a nation-state. What I am saying is that five million people are more than enough to meet each other's needs — it is possible to live a decent life with less harassment, fraud, and abuse if we work together. Each of us discovered the same pattern separately, in our own towns, jobs, and homes — and each of us was told, separately, that we were imagining it.

I am done arguing about whether it is happening. I built what comes next. Filling it is up to us.

What we have learned

The harassment is not the point. The economy behind it is.
- It runs on reward and extortion. Favors, jobs, housing, rides, and status are used to recruit ordinary people and bind them to harming us.
- Our own participation feeds it. The reason they can torture us successfully is that we depend on their infrastructure — their rides, their rentals, their platforms, their jobs. Their house, their rules. Every transaction we route through services run by people who profit from targeting extends their reach.
- Evidence alone has not ended it. Cameras, clips, and reports matter for our records, but no recording has ever shut down the machine. Cameras or not, it does not matter. What matters is their economy. That is why they can do what they do. We cannot record our way out. We have to stop paying into the market that funds our abuse.
- They mobbed us out of society. So we form our own community.

The Specterati thrive on division, shame, and isolation. The distractions — the cameras, the theatrics, the endless debates — are designed to keep us circling. The one thing that is not a distraction is where the money and labor flow.

The problems are known, and each one has an answer

Survivors compiled a list of 51 real problems we face — workplace sabotage, sudden loss of housing and jobs, vehicles and strangers that follow, financial accounts closed on false fraud claims, doctors who dismiss, mail that disappears, isolation engineered day after day.

I did not stop at the list. I built a working answer for every single one, and mapped each problem to the feature that addresses it: https://www.chargingthefuture.com/look-ma.

The answer is an economy of our own

I created the TI Skills Economy: a circular economy for survivors, where we buy from, sell to, and support each other: https://app.chargingthefuture.com/.

This is not a charity. Not a support group. Not another forum. We do not need another forum — we need infrastructure. I build and maintain the platform as a solo project. The economy it carries is all of us. One vetted, invite-only platform holds the services we would otherwise have to buy from systems used against us:
- Housing: LightHouse — verified survivor housing listings.
- Transport: TrustTransport — rides from drivers screened by the community.
- Work: Workforce and Directory — paid tasks and a skills directory across the network.
- Trade: ServiceCredits — exchange value inside the network; barter, free, or ordinary money also work.
- Help in real time: Foundation, SocketRelay, WhatWorks — tools, repairs, resource sharing, and one survivor-verified list of what actually works.
- Each other: Hub, Chyme, PeerProgramming, GentlePulse, Mood, LevelUp, Trust, ClickLog — community, live audio rooms, weekly sessions, private well-being tools, safety check-ins, and a reputation system built from real participation.

I have yet to meet a TI who is not skilled. Whether you are employed in the global economy or not has no bearing here — every member starts on equal footing. Come as you are: it does not matter how much money you have; you can contribute. Nothing in it routes value to the people who profit from targeting us. That is the whole design.

The Specterati run an economy on torture. We can run an economy on abundance. The choice is ours.

This has been done before

History has shown that oppressed people must take responsibility for their own liberation. There is no savior coming. We must come together — like it or not.

In 1903, a persecuted community in America published a book of essays called The Negro Problem — Booker T. Washington, W.E.B. Du Bois, Charles W. Chesnutt, Wilford H. Smith, and others, writing for people who were denied jobs, housing, fair courts, and physical safety by an organized system that most of the country refused to combat. The full text is free to read and download: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/15041.

Their answer was not to wait for rescue.

Washington wrote that "all races that have got upon their feet have done so largely by laying an economic foundation," and that education should be brought to bear "upon something that is needed to be done, and something which they will be permitted to do in the community." He closed with how a community answers those who doubt it: "we must re-enforce argument with results. One farm bought, one house built, one home sweetly and intelligently kept … one factory running successfully … these will tell more in our favor than all the abstract eloquence that can be summoned to plead our cause."

Du Bois opened his essay with: "The Negro race, like all races, is going to be saved by its exceptional men" — leadership developed from within, not granted from outside.

Chesnutt and Smith documented, plainly and in public, exactly how the system worked — the vote juggled away, the law dodged — so no one could claim it did not exist.

Skills. An economic foundation. Leadership from within. A public record. Results in place of argument. And it keeps working: communities in our own time have built mutual-credit economies — Switzerland's WIR network, Sardinia's Sardex — proof that people who trade with each other can hold their own inside a hostile economy. We do not compare our pain to theirs — we take the method. When the surrounding economy is used against you, build one that is not.

Our commitments

1. Refuse coercive rewards. No accepting "free" goods, services, or friendships tied to control or recruitment.
2. Use vetted services first. Route work, housing, transport, repairs, and care through the TI Skills Economy directory.
3. Document securely; do not monetize the abuse. Keep evidence for legal aid and trusted advocates, not for platforms that profit from our attention.
4. Share skills, not attention. Trade time and services inside the community instead of giving currency and views to the people harming us.
5. Stand together. Isolation is what they need to succeed. We do not isolate and we do not give up; we compare notes, witness for each other, and get what we need as a community.

The arithmetic of starting small

We do not need five million people to begin. Today, 440 people follow our Quora community; 33 survivors have created accounts on the platform, and 70 engage with the work in some capacity. My goal is to connect with the 384 who are ready. At 384, the economic model I built shows roughly $24.66 million in annual activity — a caregiver earning 32,500 a year in ServiceCredits, a mechanic 54,600, a babysitter 15,600 — real income, from and for each other, tracked openly on the network's live economic tracker.

Every repaired car, every safe ride, every hour of childcare moves value from their economy into ours. One repair, one ride, one listing — results in place of argument. The best revenge is living well, and living well together is exactly what they cannot stop. Stabilize at 384, then invite the next 1,000. Then 10,000. Then five million.

Join

1. Sign up: https://app.chargingthefuture.com/ — an email address and about two minutes.
2. List one skill or resource you can offer — fixing a sink, driving, childcare, listening.
3. Use one service from another survivor instead of buying it outside.
4. Invite one survivor you trust.

If you are at your wits' end, try one more thing — this one. What do you have to lose? They have already taken everything else. You are not required to be anyone's project or patient here. You are a member of an economy, with something to give and something to receive.

We are moving from surviving to prevailing.

Exit their economy. Exit the psyop.

Live, Work, and Prevail.

title: Why that matters for the TI Skills Economy (TSE)
content:
The Specterati's Money laundering vs. TI Skills Economy’s circular economy, why they’re not the same thing

Money laundering hides the origin of funds, so illicit cash looks legitimate. It’s a deliberate, criminal process of layering transactions, moving money through shell companies or opaque services, and finally integrating it back into the economy as “clean” money. The goal is secrecy and personal gain.

A circular economy, by contrast, is about resource efficiency and community resilience. It keeps materials and skills in use longer through repair, reuse, sharing, and local services — reducing waste, cutting costs, and strengthening local supply chains. Transparency, sustainability, and collective benefit are core principles, not concealment.

Why that matters for the TI Skills Economy (TSE)
Legitimacy: TSE’s model — connecting people who offer repair, transport, and services — is built on visible, reciprocal exchanges, not hidden financial manipulation.
 Resilience: By keeping skills and materials circulating locally, TSE reduces dependence on outside systems and builds practical autonomy for TIs.
 Ethics and trust: The circular approach fosters accountability and solidarity, while money laundering undermines trust and exposes legal risks.

Join the TI Skills Economy
If you want practical, transparent ways to regain autonomy — trade skills, find local services, and strengthen community supply chains — join TSE. Create or update your profile with the link you were sent and start connecting with nearby TIs. Every repair, ride, or shared skill adds to a resilient, self-sustaining network.

title: Time to live free
content:
Conforming to the Specterrealm (a domain ruled by fear and intimidation) that the Specterati have created is unnatural.
This is not a judgement of the plethora of TIs on Quora giving advice to the likes of “keep your head down,” stay put, work and live surrounded by the Specterati, file law suits, and barely get by for the rest of your life?
That sure is a lot of effort. Almost as much effort as the operatives of the Specterati in posing as normal people as they terrorize millions covertly 24/7/365.
Frankly I think it is time to live free, as we were intended. And to “stop” telling people about being mobbed, not so you “keep your head down,” but because most people know you are being mobbed and they do not care or will not stand up for you. They have chosen to be unfree.
The phrase "It takes a lot of effort not to be free" is a statement that challenges our conventional understanding of freedom and effort. Attributed to the philosopher Alan Watts, this idea delves into the paradoxical nature of human experience.

Watts, known for his insights into Eastern philosophy, particularly Zen Buddhism, suggests that true freedom comes from a state of being rather than from constant striving or effort. This relates to the fight against human trafficking and the "Specterati."

Understanding the Paradox
1. Effort and Freedom: Watts discussed the idea that true freedom comes from a state of being rather than from constant striving or effort. In this context, "effort" refers to the mental and emotional struggles we often engage in to control our lives, suppress our emotions, or conform to societal expectations. The more we try to control and restrict ourselves, the more effort we expend, and the less free we become.
2. Natural State: The phrase suggests that our natural state is one of freedom and spontaneity. When we try to control or suppress this natural state, we create tension and effort. In other words, it takes effort to maintain a state of unfreedom because we are constantly fighting against our natural inclinations.
3. Acceptance: Watts' teachings often emphasize acceptance and living in the present moment. By accepting ourselves and our circumstances, we can reduce the effort required to maintain a false sense of control, thereby experiencing greater freedom.
4. Paradox: The phrase is a paradox intended to challenge conventional thinking. It suggests that the more we try to control and restrict ourselves, the more effort we expend, and the less free we become. Conversely, by letting go of control and accepting our natural state, we can experience true freedom with less effort.

Applying the Paradox to Human Trafficking
The fight against human trafficking is a complex issue that requires a multifaceted approach. The phrase "It takes a lot of effort not to be free" can be applied to this context in several ways:
1. Impossible vs. Possible:
     Impossible: Thinking we will end human trafficking by pleading and talking our way out of the existence of evil people.
     Possible: Recognizing that the "Specterati"—those who operate like parasites, taking advantage of others and profiting from their suffering—are an unavoidable part of society. The only way to deter these leeches from a Target's life is by focusing on our own prosperity and building strong communities.
2. Parasites and Solutions: Parasites, like those that cause malaria or intestinal worms, need special treatment to get rid of them. Talking about them won't make them go away. We need medicine, better hygiene, and sometimes we need to get rid of where the parasites live. The legal and medical field is a byproduct of treating parasites—not the solution. Human trafficking is similar. It happens where people are vulnerable. We need to make big changes and take direct action to stop it.
Strategies to Combat the Specterati
To stop the Specterati, we need to focus on empowering individuals and building strong communities. Here are two strategies:
1. Help Targets Make Money: Give people chances to make their own money so they are not easy targets. Economic empowerment is a key factor in reducing vulnerability to exploitation.
2. Build Strong Communities: Create places where people help each other and share resources to stay safe and prosper. Strong communities can provide support and protection against exploitation.

The phrase "It takes a lot of effort not to be free" encourages a shift in perspective from one of constant effort and control to one of acceptance and natural flow. By applying this philosophy to the fight against human trafficking, we can focus on empowering individuals and building strong communities, rather than relying solely on legal and medical interventions. True freedom comes from letting go of control (fixating on the Specterati’s actions and pleading about them) and accepting our natural state, and this principle can guide us in creating a more just and equitable society.

In fact, you are not required to exchange anything with me or interact with me. It is a peer-to-peer marketplace.

The following highlights three of the mini-apps/services available: Directory, Workforce Recruiter, and Socket Relay.

Directory - create a skills profile. List all your talents, skills, and work experience in a Directory listing. Why? Now the ~5 million TIs globally can search for other TIs to exchange or do business with. For example, say you are a vet. The Speceterati will poison and torture a TI's pet. They will need to find someone who is not part of the psyop. You list in your profile that you are a vet. And now other TIs can contact you directly and pay you or barter for pet care.

Workforce Recruiter - everyone can use this as it has multiple purposes.
To have a true economy and truly thrive as Targets, we need a population with a variety of skills - every population needs this. Think about it, the Specterati are successful at human trafficking because they have people at all points of the economy/class participating globally. From the homeless to billionaires. Anecdontally, it appears that all TIs are highly skilled. But let us not worry. For example, Singapore has a population of ~5 million people, and its economy is primarily service-based. No more guessing or spreading misinformation, or having no hope about our circumstances. The data is there; either we take collective action, or we fold.

title: What is Chyme?
content:
Marketing page of the Chyme room I created for today’s Town Hall:
https://app.chargingthefuture.com/apps/chyme/room/43d5333a-1c86-462a-b600-7fbb3ccca285 All members of the TI Skills Economy have access to this dedicated product/app. And you can host your own rooms.
Chyme is a Clubhouse-style social audio Android app.
A live, drop-in audio platform where people join topic-based rooms to listen, raise hands, and speak—moderators control the stage while the audience casually discovers and hops between conversations in real time.
Social audio platforms connect people in live, drop-in audio “rooms” where conversations happen in real time.
Core concepts
- Rooms: Temporary audio spaces for a topic or event. Anyone can join as audience (listener) or participate.
- Stage / Speakers: The visible area showing current speakers and moderators. Speakers broadcast audio; moderators control the conversation.
- Audience / Listeners: Join rooms to listen, raise hands to speak, and react without speaking.
- Moderation controls: Mute/unmute, invite-to-stage, remove from room, and hand-raising queue.
- Clubs / Profiles: Persistent groups or user identities that follow interests and schedule recurring events.
Typical interactions
1. User opens app → sees list of live rooms and upcoming events.
2. User taps a room → joins as listener; sees stage and audience list.
3. Listener taps “raise hand” → moderator sees request and can promote to speaker.
4. Moderators manage conversation (mute speakers, demote to listener, remove users).
5. Room ends or user leaves; no persistent recording by default (real-time ephemeral audio).

title: What is SupportMatch?
content:
SupportMatch is an opportunity to form real bonds with other TIs with no psyop or hidden agenda.

SupportMatch randomly pairs you with others looking for a monthly accountability partner. Every 30 days—if enough people have opted in—you may receive a new match.

As matches, you mutually decide how to use your time: friendship, business collaboration, skill exchange, etc. The app includes in-app messaging and reporting features to protect your privacy. Share as much or as little as you like with your match. You are in control.

You can opt out of being matched with someone again at any time; no judgment and no reason required. If you suspect someone of abusive or predatory behavior or a member of the Specterati, please report them. We all share responsibility for removing such users.

A secure, invite-only platform designed specifically for survivors, offering essential services and support with dignity, privacy, and respect.
Service Categories
Essential Services:

Overview
This Psyop-Free Skills Economy is a comprehensive super app platform built exclusively for human trafficking survivors. Operating like WeChat’s mini-app ecosystem, it provides a unified, secure environment where survivors can access multiple essential services through a single account. Each service operates as an independent mini-app while sharing core platform functionalities, ensuring seamless integration and consistent user experience.
Key Values:


Safety First: Invite-only access with robust security measures


Privacy by Design: End-to-end encryption and data protection


Trauma-Informed: WCAG AAA accessibility standards, no overwhelming animations


Dignity & Respect: User-controlled data, complete account deletion options


Community-Driven: Built by and for survivors



Mini-Apps & Services
SupportMatch
Accountability Partner Matching
A partner matching platform featuring monthly partnership cycles, real-time messaging, and robust safety features. Connect with accountability partners for mutual support and growth.
LightHouse
Safe Housing & Accommodations
Dual-role system connecting housing seekers with hosts. Provides safe accommodations and support resources, guiding survivors towards healing and empowerment.
TrustTransport
Safe Transportation Services Request or provide safe transportation services. Connect with trusted drivers for rides to appointments, errands, or other essential travel needs.
MechanicMatch
Vehicle Repair Services
Connect with trusted mechanics for vehicle repair, remote diagnosis, or expert advice. Mechanics can build their profile and help car owners maintain safe, reliable transportation.
SocketRelay
Request & Fulfillment Network
Find what you need or help others get the goods and services they request. A community-driven mutual aid system for sharing resources.
Directory
Skill-Sharing & Collaboration
Find talented individuals to collaborate with. Build your professional profile and connect with others who share your skills and interests.
Workforce Recruiter
See distribution of skills across the Skills Economy
Track your professional profile against the needs of the community with comprehensive recruitment analytics.
LostMail
Mail Incident Reporting Report mail incidents (lost, damaged, tampered, delayed) and track your reports. Admin dashboard available for incident management and pattern tracking.
CompareNotes (Beta)
Knowledge Sharing & Q&A Post research questions, receive sourced answers, and collaboratively surface the most relevant, accurate responses with voting and tagging. Build a community knowledge base.
GentlePulse
Meditation & Wellness Library Access guided meditations hosted on Wistia, track your mood, and find supportive resources. Designed with privacy, accessibility, and trauma-informed care in mind.
Chyme (Beta)
Social Audio Platform Join private or public audio rooms for voice conversations. Secure, encrypted, and designed with privacy and trauma-informed care in mind.
Chat Groups
Real-Time Communication Access Signal.org group links for real-time chats with trusted individuals. Public listing of active groups with admin management interface.

This platform is built with care, respect, and dedication to serving the survivor community. Every feature is designed with trauma-informed principles, accessibility standards, and user dignity at the forefront.

title: There is no magic bullet
content:
There is no magic bullet

> This is not meant to shame anyone who has fallen for this or similar scams. I do not blame anyone who seeks a magic bullet. The problem is that there are no easy fixes for complex human problems. 

Magic bullet: an easy,…

This is not meant to shame anyone who has fallen for this or similar scams. I do not blame anyone who seeks a magic bullet. The problem is that there are no easy fixes for complex human problems.

Magic bullet: an easy, single solution or remedy that is expected to solve a complex problem quickly and completely. Often used skeptically to suggest such a simple fix is unrealistic.

The “cybersecurity expert’s” solution is a scam because what they propose would not remove you from the list. For starters, it assumes—without providing context or proof—that there is a specific database and that anyone can hack it and remove a name. And that database has no backup? That’s unlikely. If they don’t have permission to access the database, why would the Specterati honor the change? The list goes on: it’s absurd to claim the solution to being stalked is simply deleting a name from a database.
The earliest writings I have personally found about the Specterati date to 1690. What satellites and online databases were being used to stalk and slander targets then?
As a technical person, I should be able to clearly understand their process—after all, they created it. Non-technical people should be able to understand the message, too. But their explanation is a jumble of jargon, perhaps meant to sound technical to non-technical audiences. For the most part, no one is convinced, because the message is unclear.
“Cybersecurity experts” are promising a magic bullet. They might as well promise to deliver a unicorn.
Correct me if I’m wrong, but didn’t Nelson Mandela (paraphrased) say: it is up to the oppressed to remove the chains of oppression?

“To be free is not merely to cast off one’s chains, but to live in a way that respects and enhances the freedom of others.”

Life is not “fair,” and it doesn’t promise to be. “Cybersecurity experts” are likely perpetrators. A scammer wouldn’t enter organized crime for a measly $100 here and there from a target. Let us continue to compare notes so we can catch more of these scams and prevent people from wasting time.
How does this scam relate to the TI economy? There is no magic bullet, but we can achieve more by comparing notes and sustaining our own economy: exiting the psyop.
The Specterati is a multi-generational organized crime ring. It does not rely on a single copy of a “database.” You have been doxed to a global network of narc grifters who would put their own children on the list if it would preserve whatever they want.
By perps framing the problem as a single line in a database, it further keeps Targets in an endless endeavor of fixating on their mind games. Empowering Change: Start Your Own Service-Based Business
With a market of 5 million Targeted Individuals (TIs), starting your own service-based business is not just a dream—it’s a real opportunity. Our new app, the Workforce Recruiter, helps you find out what skills are needed in our community. Here’s how it can work for you.

Why You Can Start Your Own Service-Based Business


Community Needs Matter:
Your community may have many needs that aren’t being met. By looking at these gaps, you can offer services or products that help your neighbors. Whether it’s tutoring, home repairs, or wellness coaching, your skills can provide valuable solutions.


Tap Into a Global Market:
Our app shows where skills are in demand, both locally and around the world. With insights into where your talents can be useful, you can focus on jobs that are important but not too crowded with competition. For example, if you target just 1% of the market, that’s 50,000 potential customers.


Empowerment Through Skills:
Many people have skills that often go unnoticed. By using the Workforce Recruiter, you can discover what you are good at and how those skills fit into a bigger picture. This is about more than just earning money; it’s about taking charge of your life and finding independence.


Inspiration from Successful Models:
Countries like Singapore, Finland, and Norway have populations of around 5 million and thrive through different sectors like technology, agriculture, and innovation. Their success can inspire you to know what’s possible in your own business journey.


Sustainable Livelihoods:
Our goal is to create a skills economy that supports individuals and helps vulnerable communities, including those affected by human trafficking. By focusing on skill sharing and helping one another, we can build a community where everyone has a chance to succeed.



How the App Works
The Workforce Recruiter keeps track of hiring trends across various sectors within the TI economy. It looks at job roles based on skill levels and training needs so you can understand what skills are popular and where more are needed.


Identify Gaps: The app helps you find specific skills that are needed but not currently available, allowing you to target those areas for your business.


Global Perspective: The app tracks the TI Skills Economy globally, giving you insights from around the world.



The Call to Action
Now is the perfect time to take action! By using the Workforce Recruiter, you can explore what services are most needed in our community. Let’s work together to build a strong service-based economy where we help each other create sustainable livelihoods.
Every skill counts, and every effort matters. Let’s empower ourselves and each other to succeed in our own service-based businesses. Your talents can make a difference—let’s turn them into opportunities today!

Market Size and Viability for a Small Business with a Population Size of 5 Million
A market size of 5 million people can indeed support a successful service-based small business, provided certain conditions are met. Here’s a breakdown of the rationale behind this.
Key Considerations for Viability


Target Market Identification:

If you can identify and effectively target a niche within this market, even a small portion can produce substantial revenue. For instance, if you target just 1% of the market, that’s 50,000 potential customers.



Service Demand:

The success of a service-based business also hinges on the demand for your specific services. Consider whether the services meet a significant need, such as health, beauty, home services, or consulting.



Pricing Strategy:

Higher-value services can yield greater revenue with fewer clients. If your service can charge $100 per session, for example, serving 50 clients per month can generate $5,000 monthly.



Competition:

Evaluate the competitive landscape. A market that is underserved may present better opportunities than a saturated one, even within a population of 5 million.



Operational Costs:

Consider the overhead involved. If operational costs are manageable, it’s feasible to sustain a profit. This includes rent, materials, staffing, and marketing.



Marketing and Outreach:

Your ability to effectively market your services to the target audience impacts how well you can tap into the 5 million population. Utilizing digital marketing, social media, and community engagement can enhance visibility.



Scalability:

Many service-based businesses have the potential to scale. As you build a customer base, you might introduce additional services or expand to new areas, resulting in increased profits.



Economic Environment:

Factors such as economic health, disposable income levels, and consumer spending habits in the area can greatly affect business viability



Conclusion
A 5 million population is substantial enough to support a service-based small business, provided you have a clear understanding of your niche, the demand for your services, and an effective strategy for reaching your target customers. The key is to ensure your offerings align with market needs while managing operational costs to maximize profitability. With the right approach, it’s entirely possible to make a good living in this environment.

And so it’s not necessarily a failure by any means, but since the group chat is very intimate, it provides a better way for people to connect instantly.
And I was thinking how can I kind of do a simpler version of Craigslist to match the energy of the group chat. And so that’s why I added the new feature today, SocketRelay. It allows an individual in 140 characters or less to state what they need, and someone can click a button instantly say, hey, I got what you need and send it to you. It is on the transactional side of things, but I think that having that specific feature be super transactional, gives the ability for people to build trust faster. And so I’m definitely looking for feedback on it, please let me know.
Lastly, there is Sleep Stories, which was released earlier in the month. It’s a hobby of mine to practice meditation. And I heard that Calm Sleep Stories is something that’s super popular. And I like to listen to stuff to fall asleep. Creating custom stories that relate to our daily lives would be very helpful. And so I created psyop-free Sleep Stories for you all.
Go to app.chargingthefuture.com to access the TI economy. Remember that it is invite-only, but it only takes a moment. What you do is click to register, and it takes less than a minute. Once you’re signed up, it’s going to ask for an invite code. DM me on any platform, whether it’s Discourse, Quora, or Signal for the code. I’ll give you the code, you’ll then be able to register immediately.
You don’t have to register under your real identity if you don’t want to. But keep in mind, there are some services that will expose it. For example, if you’re looking for housing, you will eventually reveal your identity to individuals. But I don’t ask for any of that information. I don’t even ask for your cell phone. The whole goal is to build a platform that is trusted, that TIs can go to, that is PsyOp-free, and Perp-free. I’ve said this multiple times on Quora, but there was another TI that shared that there were about 2 million self-reports of targeted individuals to the United Nations. My guess is that number is cumulative.
Imagine if there are 2 million people who self-reported, and I’m a person who hasn’t self-reported. This means there’s definitely way more than just those individuals. And so looking at different crime rates, they usually say that crimes are about 50% under-reported. If there are 2 million people who are saying that they’re targeted individuals, you can imagine that there are at least 2 million additional. And so with that, that’s the size of a small nation state. And so for us to come together would mean that we’d be able to get the resources that we need amongst each other.
I really appreciate all the individuals who have joined so far. And at any time, if you have any questions, you can send me a message on Signal, you can also reach me on Quora and Discourse. Thank you again for joining the TownHall, or should I say listening to this recording of the Town Hall. And I hope that you’ll be able to join live at some point in the future.
