Welcome to the Townhall audio recap. I go live at least once a week. Last week, I used Signal, but it was a clunky experience. Today, I went live a few times on Twitch, which went pretty well. However, when live-streaming on mobile, you can’t multitask, which was an odd experience. Some people joined, but they don’t seem to be followers, and no one interacted in the chat. It’s unclear if the attendees were Targeted Individuals, perpetrators, or just random viewers.
The purpose of this recording is to provide a brief recap of the live. I will post the transcript of this recording on the blog post, which also contains a similar recap. The reason for this audio recording is to offer varied ways to get updates about the TI economy.
During the Townhall, I mentioned there were a few major updates compared to last week. The intention of the Town Hall is to allow live interaction with me, providing better social proof. This helps demonstrate that I am a genuine targeted individual, not a perpetrator, which supports community building and access to necessary resources.
This week, there are three major updates. I always make small tweaks; for example, I added dark mode to the app, but those are just minor stylistic changes. Today’s Townhall focused only on the major updates.
Last week, I announced the creation of the TI economy super app containing many apps in one place for easier access to different resources. This week I added a page (not necessarily a mini-app) listing all the Signal chat groups in a single page. Now, you can just go to one link that has all the resources and chat groups reducing confusion on what link can get you what you need or want.
The second major change is the launch of a new mini-app called Directory. Historically, all disenfranchised groups want a directory. Many TIs would like a directory to connect with other TIs, exchange resources, and goods. The Directory has a clean interface. When you create a profile, you can choose to make some information publicly available. This creates a shareable link to your directory profile, which provides a preview of your profile. You can post this link in your Quora bio or share it in social media posts, allowing others to see a part of your profile. This is useful because the app is invite-only, and you must be logged in to see most of the content. By having a shareable link with selective information, it helps potential new members preview the app before deciding to join. While increasing your exposure to more TIs that you can build a meaningful relationship with.
The last major update is the mini-app called SocketRelay, which I announced last week. It allows you to quickly request a resource in 140 characters. Inspired by an incident where a perp stolen my winter jacket and I vented about the experience in the Signal chat group. A TI immediately helped me by sending a coat and a jacket after mine was stolen. I wanted to recreate that supportive interaction in a more public setting. Now, when you create a request in SocketRelay, and opt to make it public, generating a shareable link. This link can be posted on Facebook, other social media, or Quora, expanding the reach for getting the resources you need. This public feature is optional.
These are the three major changes since last week’s Town Hall. If you have any questions, you can leave them on Quora, send a message on Signal, or reply directly within the blog post on the Town Square forum.
The link to the app is app.chargingthefuture.com, where you can access everything. I hope you can join future live streams. I try to accommodate as many time zones as possible, which is why I go online throughout the entire day. For the foreseeable future, I’ll stick to streaming on Twitch. My Twitch handle is the1690s (https://www.twitch.tv/the1690s), chosen because of a historical reference to the Specterati from the year 1690. It doesn’t have any specific significance beyond that; it was just a quick choice for a handle.
Hopefully, the new features are valuable to you, and I am always open to feedback on what features you want or any new mini-apps you would like to see. Just let me know.
